page: Microsoft Azure D48_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine hypervised by Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.8 GHz. The instance allocates 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 24 physical cores with two threads per core. Memory capacity totals 192.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The processor architecture includes 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI, along with hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance provides no bundled local ephemeral storage and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring remote network-attached disks for persistence.

Benchmark results place the D48_v5 in the middle 50 percent for general single-core and multi-core processing, scoring 1,899.19 in stress-ng single-core and 46,526.02 in stress-ng multi-core tests, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 15,152.0. Memory subsystem testing shows strong results, achieving a PassMark memory score of 2,788.8 and uncached large-block read bandwidth of 150.16 GB/sec. The presence of VAES and SHA-NI instructions yields strong performance in cryptographic workloads, scoring 42,240.46 in the PassMark encryption test, as well as a strong Geekbench image processing score of 14,757.0. Without discrete GPU accelerators, CPU-bound LLM text generation scales down significantly as model sizes increase, reaching 22.45 tokens per second on a 7B parameter model and 2.62 tokens per second on a 70B parameter model.

The instance provides balanced resource density suitable for multi-threaded enterprise applications that do not require local NVMe temporary scratch disks. Due to its balanced compute-to-memory ratio, high cryptographic throughput, and memory bandwidth, the D48_v5 fits enterprise application hosting, relational database engines, static web serving clusters, large compilation jobs, and multi-threaded ETL pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure D48_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. It is provisioned with 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores, 192.0 GB of system memory, and a 48 MB L3 cache. The architecture maintains a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with no bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware. In benchmark tests, the instance demonstrates mid-tier multi-core computing metrics alongside strong cryptographic execution and high memory throughput, supported by AVX-512 VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI instruction set extensions. Workloads lacking hardware acceleration, such as large-scale LLM generation, show expected CPU limitations. The balanced allocation of compute and system memory makes the D48_v5 suitable for relational database servers, enterprise web applications, software compilation pipelines, and containerized backend microservices relying on remote storage.
